comparator.name: Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 Leiden study product defines a 180-EC Physics bachelor: a 60-EC compulsory first year, 51 EC of compulsory second-year physics and mathematics plus 9 EC of restricted physics choices, and a third year with a 30-EC elective/core-package space, a separate 3-EC restricted physics choice and a 27-EC bachelor research project. To instantiate one coherent physics-centred pathway, the second-year 9 EC selects Astro-Particle Physics (6 EC) and Fluid Phenomena in Soft Matter (3 EC); the third-year 30-EC core package selects the first five remaining 6-EC physics options in official order, and the separate 3 EC selects Relativistic Electrodynamics. These choices preserve the published rules and are made independently of UCR fit. The university’s public programme pages describe the same theoretical-and-experimental foundation, free-specialisation semester and culminating independent physics research project.

exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Physics bachelor’s defining sequence of mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical and solid-state physics, repeated experimental laboratories and a 27-EC independent physics research project. The current UCR catalogue contains mathematics, programming and energy/sustainability courses but no physics course sequence or physics laboratory. Filling the remaining places with adjacent mathematics, data science, engineering or sustainability courses would change the target into a different interdisciplinary programme and falsely imply foundational and advanced physics training that UCR does not provide.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: 60 EC compulsory first year; 51 EC compulsory second year plus an instantiated 9-EC restricted physics choice; and 30 EC of instantiated physics core-package options, a separate 3-EC physics choice, and a 27-EC bachelor research project in year three. The programme has no named graduation route, so routeSelection is null. Its academic identity is sustained theoretical, mathematical and experimental physics rather than a collection of broadly science-related electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. UCR offers DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics, as well as DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming. Those courses provide useful mathematical and computational tools, but the catalogue contains no course in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, solid-state physics, astrophysics or experimental physics, and no physics laboratory or physics research sequence. ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design concern energy systems and sustainable design rather than foundational physics. Even the strongest adjacent set therefore cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Physics rationale or reproduce the external programme’s theory–experiment progression.
